newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO sees closer links with new E.Europe partners.
newsitem.headline: NATO sees closer links with new E.Europe partners.

text.p: NATO's top military officials said on Friday that the alliance's partner countries in eastern Europe and elsewhere should be brought closer to NATO planning as part of the next stage of forging links with the old enemy.

A meeting of defence chiefs of staff from the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation said that an enhanced Partnership for Peace (PFP) programme should include having officers from partner countries in NATO headquarters across Europe.
German General Klaus Naumann said the idea was to bring PFP countries into planning discussions, offering "more than liaison" but stopping short of actually appointing any PFP officers to posts.
"We will not offer jobs.... They will be inside the fence, but they will not be part of the integrated military structure," he said.
The PFP concept was agreed by NATO's 16 countries as a way of developing links with former Warsaw Pact countries such as Poland and Hungary, and with European neutrals such as Finland.
For the most part, PFP has involved having liaison officers at various NATO centres, including at the Brussels headquarters, and conducting joint excercises.

Most of the former Communist PFP countries have said they want to join NATO. The decision on which countries will be invited in first -- expected to be Poland, Hungary, the Czech republic and possibly Slovenia -- will be made next year.
